Entry 4401B: Patient admitted to Bellevue, 1923, complaining of persistent memory of own funeral. Hospital records confirm patient died during routine surgery. Patient discharged self three days later, arguing with death certificate.

Weather station log, Wyoming 1887: Temperature recorded as 40F during July heatwave. Thermometer functioned normally for all other readings. Cattle found frozen in pasture while grass remained green beneath them.

Archaeological survey, Pompeii 79 CE: Bakery oven contained perfectly preserved pizza with toppings unknown to Roman cuisine. Pineapple cultivation begins 1200 years later. Cheese variety still unidentified by food historians.

Digital surveillance footage, London Metro 2003: Platform cameras record same commuter boarding 7:42 AM train for fourteen consecutive days. Transport records show train service discontinued in 1997. Station demolished 1999.

Biological survey, Amazon Basin 1892: Botanist catalogs flowering vine that blooms backwards into seed, then sapling, then nothing. Local guides refuse to approach plant, claim it steals years from tomorrow.

Census records, Byzantine Empire 1143: Population of Thessalonica includes 847 citizens listed as temporarily elsewhere in when. Tax collectors report difficulty locating these individuals across correct centuries.

Personal diary, Edinburgh 1794: Woman records conversation with her reflection, who claims to be living in 1923. Mirror belonged to clockmaker who died during conversation. Both women describe identical room furnishings.

Geological survey, Pleistocene epoch: Mammoth remains, 40,000 BCE, found with titanium hip replacement. Surgical technique matches 1980s orthopedic standards. Bone healing indicates mammoth lived additional 12 years postsurgery.

Digital artifact 2009: Smartphone recovered from Pompeii ash layer, 79 CE. Device contains 14,000 photos of eruption from multiple angles impossible for single observer. Battery at 23, still functional.

Herbarium specimen, Royal Gardens 1823: Pressed flower identified as common daisy, collected July 15th. Botanical analysis reveals species won't evolve for another 200 years. Collector's notes describe field that existed only on Wednesdays.

Census data, Constantinople 1453: Population records list 847 residents who don't cast shadows. Tax assessments calculated at halfrate. Municipal lamplighter reports streets remain dark even at noon in affected districts.

Great Zimbabwe, c. 1360:
A loft of 62 pigeons is established to announce the new moon to the hill villages.
The pigeons are fed on the new moon only, to make them punctual.
By the next rains the moon has been rescheduled for whenever the pigeons are fed.
coined: The loft at the Hill Enclosure

text: Hear it in every market of the Caliphate: the Counters of Dusk shall continue to levy one cowrie per household for the long evening of Zaria. The evening ended in 1783. The cowries have not been told.

coined: The lending of the Debre Damo rope
